questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars appears red because its surface is rich in iron oxide, commonly known as rust.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Gold's symbol Au comes from its Latin name 'aurum'. Ag is silver, from 'argentum'.
questions.mnemonic: 'Aurum' — A for the first letter pair AU of gold.

questions.question: Who wrote the play 'Romeo and Juliet'?
questions.explanation: William Shakespeare wrote 'Romeo and Juliet' around 1595 as a tragedy about two young lovers.
questions.mnemonic: Shake a spear at the star-crossed lovers.

questions.question: How many continents are there on Earth?
questions.explanation: There are seven continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.
questions.mnemonic: A-A-N-S-A-E-A — seven letters for seven continents.

questions.question: Which gas do plants primarily absorb for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.
questions.mnemonic: Photosynthesis takes IN Carbon — 'CO2 in, O2 out'.

questions.question: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of the Earth's surface.
questions.mnemonic: Pacific = 'Peaceful' and the biggest of them all.

questions.question: In which year did India gain independence?
questions.explanation: India became independent from British rule on 15 August 1947.

questions.question: What is the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's energy in the form of ATP, hence called the powerhouse.

questions.question: Which is the smallest prime number?
questions.explanation: 2 is the smallest prime number and the only even prime.
questions.mnemonic: Two is tiny and even — the only even prime.

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa in the early 16th century.
questions.mnemonic: da Vinci — the 'Renaissance Man' behind the smiling lady.

questions.question: What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest known natural material, scoring 10 on the Mohs scale.
questions.mnemonic: Diamonds are forever — and hardest of all.

questions.question: How many bones are there in the adult human body?
questions.explanation: An adult human body has 206 bones. Babies are born with about 270, many of which fuse together.
